Reviews are still running. Summary of where things stand while I wait:

**The bug and the fix.** The Documents tab on a person's profile is the Document Library component mounted inside the profile page. The page knew the person's id instantly (it's in the URL) but the signed-in elder only arrived a moment later from Firebase. The tab mounted in that gap and copied the user as "nobody", permanently. Creating a document then read an id off nobody and threw.

It now gets a *reader* for identity instead of a copy, so it always sees whatever the page currently knows. That fixes the crash and the quieter bug behind it — every document created there would otherwise have been signed "Elder" rather than by the elder who wrote it.

**What else changed.** The document record is now assembled by a plain function in the shared core rather than inline in a click handler, and it refuses to build a document with no author at all. The failure message now says which thing went wrong instead of six generic words.

**Tests.** Ten new tests on the builder, six on the wiring. I checked both go red against the old code and green against the fix. Full suite: 2695 pass, 7 fail — all seven fail identically before my changes, so none are mine (they're a missing Tailwind package and some mobile/calendar tests).

I'll report the review findings when they land.

**Agreement — the core of the fix.** The new `Author` entry (CONTEXT.md lines 656-657) — "a document whose author cannot be resolved is refused rather than written, because an untraceable pastoral record is worse than a create that failed" — matches the code almost word for word: `refuseUnauthored`/`MISSING_AUTHOR` in `public/shepherding-documents-core.js:132-141`, and the same rationale repeated in the docstring above `buildElderDocument` (lines 163-165) and in `test/shepherding-documents-author.test.js:6-8`. `author` as a getter (`shepherding-documents.js:299-304`) is exactly the `{uid, name}` shape the model names. No drift here.

The rewritten **Elder Document** entry ("Created either in the Document Library, where it belongs to no Person, or on a Person's Shepherding Profile, where it does (ADR-0015)", line 652) now correctly matches ADR-0015's decision 2-4 (`ownerPersonId` on profile-scoped documents). That correction is right.

**Invention — ADR-0015's contract is now stale.** ADR-0015 decision 2 (line 33-36) fixes the `documentLibrary` config as `{ structureDocId, ownerPersonId, embedded }`. The fix adds a fourth key, `identity`, both at the call site (`public/shepherding-profile.html:1041`: `identity: () => ({ user: currentUser, name: currentUserName, permissionLevel: currentPermissionLevel })`) and in the component (`shepherding-documents.js:32`: `readHostIdentity: typeof config.identity === 'function' ? config.identity : null`). This is a real, load-bearing change to a documented interface — CONTEXT.md's `Document Library` entry (lines 668-673) doesn't mention it either. ADR-0015 §2 should be amended (or a short follow-on ADR added) to record the `identity` reader as part of the contract, the same way the rest of this project gives small standalone decisions their own ADR (e.g. ADR-0032, ADR-0034). The refusal behaviour itself (`MISSING_AUTHOR`) is likewise a new invariant recorded only in CONTEXT.md's `Author` entry, not in any ADR — worth the same treatment for consistency, though not a contradiction.

**Minor collision.** CONTEXT.md already uses "identity" for a different concept — a Shepherding Tag's stable identity across a Rename (line 301: "preserving its identity"). The code's new `identity`/`ownIdentity`/`readHostIdentity` (`shepherding-documents.js:32-42`) is an unrelated sense — the signed-in user. Not currently confusing since the two live in different files/domains, but it's the exact kind of word reuse CONTEXT.md's `_Avoid_` lists exist to head off, and worth a one-line disambiguating note if a future entry ever needs to name it explicitly.

No renamed-but-undocumented model terms found otherwise; `MISSING_AUTHOR`, `refuseUnauthored`, `requiredText`, `readHostIdentity`, `ownIdentity`, `createFailureMessage` are implementation-only identifiers with no corresponding (or conflicting) model term, which is fine — CONTEXT.md doesn't name every helper, only ones that carry domain meaning, and none of these do.

The house convention is an inline `*Amended (MS-XXX).*` note. Following it.

## Correctness sweep (the getter-only question) — CLEAR

No code anywhere assigns `currentUser` / `currentUserName` / `currentPermissionLevel` on the `documentLibrary` component. The ~12 other hits (`shepherding-profile.js`, `shepherding-people.js`, `admin-dashboard.js`, …) are separate Alpine components with their own data. Only two mounts exist; neither `x-model`s these. Alpine 3.15 standard build keeps object-literal getters through `reactive()`, and the arrow in the mount closes over the `with`-scope proxy, so it re-reads live. `auth.js` is loaded on `shepherding-profile.html`, so the `typeof auth` fallback resolves.

## Findings

**1. HARD — the second copy was not converted.** `public/mobile/data.js:729` `createElderDocument` builds the identical record inline and still carries *both* bugs this change exists to kill:
```js
var name = (user && user.name) || "Elder";
var uid = (user && user.uid) || (auth.currentUser && auth.currentUser.uid) || null;
```
CONTEXT.md now asserts "**Every Elder Document has one**" — mobile writes `authorUid: null` and author "Elder" happily. Duplicated Code / Shotgun Surgery. The two copies have also *diverged*: mobile prefers `filterId`, the new builder prefers `filterConfig`.

**2. Judgement — the `author` uid fallback is dead weight.** `auth.currentUser` rescues the uid, but `name` has no fallback and the builder requires both. If host identity is empty, name is `''` and it refuses anyway. "Belt and braces" that only covers a case that cannot occur.

**3. Judgement — Duplicated Code in `createDocument`.** `this.createFilterMode === 'preset'` is evaluated twice on adjacent lines, and the same preset-vs-custom choice is made *again* inside `buildElderDocument`. Two places own one rule. `{ ...this.customFilter }` is spread in the caller and re-spread in the builder.

**4. Judgement — Primitive Obsession.** `e.code === 'permission-denied'` is a bare literal beside the exported `Docs.MISSING_AUTHOR`.

**5. Judgement — file convention.** `shepherding-documents-core.js` uses only `//` comments; `buildElderDocument` adds the file's sole `/** */` JSDoc. Same change writes "ADR-0015" in CONTEXT.md but "ADR 0015" in core.js; repo majority is hyphenated. ADR-0015 §1 covers *tree* logic, not the record — the citation is a stretch.

**6. Judgement — test conventions.** `document-library-identity-wiring.test.js` uses loose `assert.deepEqual`; its sibling `shepherding-documents-author.test.js` uses `deepStrictEqual`. The comment on line 63 claims the regex matches "`key:` anything that is not a function" — it does no such check and would flag `currentUser:` inside a legitimate reader.

**7. Judgement, adjacent.** `shepherding-profile.js:868, 992, 1174` still do unguarded `this.currentUser.uid` on the same page. Same fault class, uncovered.

## Verdict: substantially meets the spec. Two partial gaps, two implementation smells. No scope creep.

**Traced answers to your questions**

(a) **Equivalent, exactly.** Old: `createFilterMode === 'preset' ? filterId = selectedViewId : filterConfig = {...customFilter}`. New passes `filterId: preset ? selectedViewId : null` / `filterConfig: preset ? null : customFilter`, and the builder branches on `if (filterConfig)`. `customFilter` is initialised and reset to a literal object (lines 65, 292), so it is never falsy — the non-preset branch always lands on `filterConfig`. Preset with `selectedViewId === null` (no views) writes `filterId: null`, same as before. No input crosses over.

(b) Yes. `updatedByName` = `authorName` (was `currentUserName`); `allDocs` entry uses `docData.authorName`. Same values, now trimmed.

(c) Yes. `createFolder` → `saveStructure` touches no identity field.

(d) Yes. `ownIdentity` is assigned before `ShepherdingBlur.configure`, which reads `this.currentPermissionLevel` — resolves through the getter to the real level.

(e) One remaining reader: `finishRename` (line 402). See finding 3.

(f) Refusal fires on null/undefined/`{}`/empty/whitespace uid *and* name; `buildElderDocument` is the only assembler and throws before returning, so no path reaches `db.add` unauthored.

**(a) Criteria partly met**

1. *"The created document's author name is the signed-in Elder's name, NOT the literal string 'Elder'."* The fallback was removed from the embedded component but not from the host: `shepherding-profile.js:314-316` still resolves to `'Elder'` when the user record has no email. Normal case is fixed; the literal can still be written.
2. *MS-296: "full suite passes."* 7 failures — but all 7 are present on a clean tree (missing `@tailwindcss/forms`, `mobile-relationships-tab`). Not caused by this change. Both new files pass (16 tests).

**(c) Implemented, but looks wrong**

3. *MS-294: "the create path resolves the uid at call time falling back to the live auth session."* The `author` getter falls back to `auth.currentUser` for **uid only** — `name` still comes from `this.currentUserName`. If the host user is null, the fallback supplies a uid, the name is `''`, and the builder refuses anyway. The belt-and-braces can never actually rescue a create.
4. *MS-293: "loading/browsing documents on the tab behaves exactly as before."* Removing the `'Elder'` embedded fallback means `finishRename` now writes `updatedByName: ''` instead of `'Elder'` in the pre-auth window. Low risk (a rename needs a loaded list), but it is a silently-empty field where a string used to be.

**(b) Scope creep:** none of substance. `requiredText` trims the author **uid**, which nobody asked for; harmless.

**Done — MS-283 is in review.** PR #30, branch `MS-283`, all four sub-tasks closed.

The Documents tab on a person's profile is the Document Library dropped inside the profile page, and the page was handing it a *copy* of who's signed in. The person's id sits in the web address, so it's there instantly; the signed-in elder turns up a moment later. The tab mounted in that gap, copied "nobody", and kept it. Every attempt to make a document then failed on that, before anything even reached the database — and the error message said six generic words, which is why the demo had nothing to go on.

It now gets a *reader* rather than a copy, so it always sees whatever the page currently knows. That also fixed a quieter one hiding underneath: the elder's name was frozen at the same bad moment but had a fallback, so every document made there would have been signed "Elder" instead of by whoever wrote it — no error, no clue.

Two guards on top. The document record is now built by a plain function in the shared code that refuses to make one with no author at all, and the failure message says which thing went wrong.

**Tests.** 21 new ones. There's no way to test a browser page here, so the logic is tested at the new seam and the wiring gets a test that reads the source — the same trick an existing test uses for a similar invisible bug. I checked both go red against the old code. Suite is 2700 passing; the 7 failures are all pre-existing and fail the same way on a clean checkout.

**Two things I left, both needing your call:**

1. The **mobile app has the same bug** in its own copy of this code — signs "Elder", writes a blank author. The ticket ruled mobile out on the basis that it "already handles identity correctly", which is true elsewhere but not for this one function. I didn't widen into it, but it means the glossary now promises something one path can still break.
2. `shepherding-profile.js` has three more unguarded reads of the signed-in user, same fault, same page. Lower risk, since they only run after you click something.
